title: Biomarkers decoded — the 'normal labs' myth (ferritin)
caption:
Myth: normal bloodwork means your iron is fine. Truth: a CBC doesn't measure ferritin — your iron stores. WHO 2020: under 15 µg/L is depleted.
Save this for your next appointment. Which myth next? 👇
www.aiforheratx.org
#ferritin #irondeficiency #womenshealth #heavyperiods #biomarkers

scenes.text: Always *exhausted* — but they keep telling me my labs are normal?

scenes.text: A standard CBC measures hemoglobin, not *ferritin* — so your iron savings can be empty while the report says normal.
phrases: The myth: "normal labs" means nothing is wrong.
A standard CBC checks hemoglobin — today's iron in the blood.
Ferritin is different: it is your iron *savings account*.
You can run that account to empty and still read 'normal.'

scenes.text: She typed three words into her phone — *ferritin*, TSH, B12 — and asked for them by name at her next appointment.
phrases: Write down three asks: ferritin, TSH, B12 — and say them out loud.
Eat lentils or spinach with lemon or peppers; vitamin C helps you absorb iron (NIH Office of Dietary Supplements).
Walk 30 minutes on most days — that is the WHO's 150 minutes a week.
